abstract: Let $A$ be nonzero in the cohomology ring of a smooth projective toric variety $X$. In this note, we observe the existence of a nonzero Gromov-Witten invariant of the form $\langle A, A, \ldots\rangle_{0, n,\beta}^X$ as a consequence of Iritani's work on the big quantum cohomology ring of $X$. This implies Koll\'ar's conjecture on the symplectic deformation invariance of rational connectedness in the case where $X$ is toric. If $X$ is moreover Fano and $B$ is also nonzero in the cohomology ring, we prove the existence of a nonzero Gromov-Witten invariant of the form $\langle A,B,*\rangle_{0,3,\beta}^X$ using Batyrev's presentation of the small quantum cohomology ring of $X$. We conclude with a few consequences of this nonvanishing result.
hook: Toric varieties always have a nonzero Gromov-Witten invariant, settling Kollar's conjecture for them.
summary: For smooth projective toric varieties, the author shows that any nonzero cohomology class appears in a nonzero Gromov-Witten invariant, using Iritani's work on quantum cohomology. This settles Kollar's conjecture on symplectic deformation invariance of rational connectedness for toric cases. It applies to toric varieties only.
title: Gromov-Witten Nonvanishing and Symplectic Deformations of Toric Varieties
